themes: Cost transformation delivering Rs 2,900 cr traceable improvements; 98% 1Q compliance to plan across geographies
Kalinganagar ramp-up on track: CAL grade approvals secured, CGL first coil June 2025, steelmaking facilities complete by Q1
China exporting 9-10MT monthly creating trade volatility; India price pressure from early monsoons; recovery expected post-monsoon
UK EAF transition with Port Talbot groundbreaking started; targeting £150/ton cost decline and breakeven by FY2026 end
NINL blast furnace operations resumed post-maintenance; expansion FID target Oct-Nov 2025 after environment clearance completion
Ludhiana EAF model leveraging local scrap, 300km local sell radius, Rs 2-3k per ton transport savings vs Jamshedpur
risks: China exports 9-10 million tons monthly creating regional trade flow volatility and Indian price pressure despite safeguard duties
UK automotive demand down 15% YoY; safeguard quotas exceed domestic demand causing UK-Germany price divergence vs prior policy intent
US tariff uncertainty and melt-and-pour dispute with UK affecting EAF model; trade deal impacts on EU-US not finalized
European capacity utilization only 60-65%; multiple green steel projects delayed (SSAB 1-1.5 year delay); industry restructuring ongoing

analyst_pushback.analyst_pushback: Sumangal (Kotak): Why no Board approval for NINL expansion given Kalinganagar ramp-up timeline?
analyst_pushback.management_response: Changed process: complete engineering and environment clearance before FID ensuring execution readiness, avoiding earlier delays post-approval

analyst_pushback.analyst_pushback: Satyadeep (Ambit): Why pursue UK transition when quota issues existed at decision time?
analyst_pushback.management_response: US tariff actions and China export surge post-Jan 2025 materially changed dynamics; EU already revised quotas; UK more receptive now

analyst_pushback.analyst_pushback: Ashish (Macquarie): Only marginal QoQ EBITDA growth despite Rs 2,900 cr cost savings?
analyst_pushback.management_response: Without cost savings EBITDA would have declined due to lower volumes; YoY visibility clearer; 85% savings traceable to P&L

analyst_pushback.analyst_pushback: Amit (Axis): Can NINL expansion achieve 24-month execution timeline?
analyst_pushback.management_response: 3-3.5 years more realistic for integrated plant vs 2 years for Ludhiana; leveraging Kalinganagar experience and parallel execution

tone_evidence: Confident on cost transformation and long-term strategy; cautious on near-term India pricing and UK automotive demand; defensive on regulatory uncertainties (CBAM, tariffs)
